headline: Tanzid Hasan scores century; Bangladesh hit 100s in all Test-playing nations
summary: From Aminul Islam's debut century in 2000 to Tanzid Hasan's feat in Australia, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in every Test-playing country.
details: Tanzid Hasan's century in Australia in 2026 marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket, completing the circle of centuries scored in all Test-playing nations.
The journey began in November 2000 in Dhaka, where Aminul Islam scored a century in Bangladesh's inaugural Test match.
Following this, Mohammad Ashraful recorded the first overseas century for Bangladesh in 2001 in Sri Lanka, which remains the youngest player to score a Test century.
Habibul Bashar achieved the feat in Pakistan in 2003 and in the West Indies in 2004, becoming the first Bangladeshi batsman to score centuries in two different continents.
In 2010, the list grew with Mahmudullah scoring a century in New Zealand and Tamim Iqbal scoring a century in England, including a historic hundred at Lord's.
Mushfiqur Rahim's century in India in 2017 was widely regarded as one of the best overseas innings for the country.
Bangladesh finally achieved a century in Zimbabwe in 2021, with Mahmudullah, Sadman Islam, and Nazmul Hossain scored hundreds in Harare.
Mahmudul Hasan Joy scored the only century for Bangladesh in South Africa in 2022 in Durban.
With Tanzid Hasan's century in Australia, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in the other Test-playing nations, except for Afghanistan and Ireland, where they have not yet played a match.
This achievement completes a long journey that started with home ground success and has completed in one of the world's toughest cricketing environments.
caption:
From Dhaka to Darwin, the circle is complete. Bangladesh has now scored centuries in every Test-playing nation they have played in!

Tanzid Hasan's century in Australia in 2026 marks a historic milestone for Bangladesh cricket, completing the circle of centuries scored in all Test-playing nations.

The journey began in November 2000 in Dhaka, where Aminul Islam scored a century in Bangladesh's inaugural Test match.

Following this, Mohammad Ashraful recorded the first overseas century for Bangladesh in 2001 in Sri Lanka, which remains the youngest player to score a Test century.

Habibul Bashar achieved the feat in Pakistan in 2003 and in the West Indies in 2004, becoming the first Bangladeshi batsman to score centuries in two different continents.

In 2010, the list grew with Mahmudullah scoring a century in New Zealand and Tamim Iqbal scoring a century in England, including a historic hundred at Lord's.

Mushfiqur Rahim's century in India in 2017 was widely regarded as one of the best overseas innings for the country.

Bangladesh finally achieved a century in Zimbabwe in 2021, with Mahmudullah, Sadman Islam, and Nazmul Hossain scored hundreds in Harare.

Mahmudul Hasan Joy scored the only century for Bangladesh in South Africa in 2022 in Durban.

With Tanzid Hasan's century in Australia, Bangladesh has now scored centuries in the other Test-playing nations, except for Afghanistan and Ireland, where they have not yet played a match.

This achievement completes a long journey that started with home ground success and has completed in one of the world's toughest cricketing environments.

headline_marked: Opposition leader [[urges special parliament session]] over energy crisis
headline: Opposition leader urges special parliament session over energy crisis
summary: Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has written to the acting president requesting an urgent session to address severe electricity and fuel shortages across Bangladesh.
details: Opposition leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has written to Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed calling for a special session of the National Parliament.
The request comes amid a severe electricity and fuel crisis that has led to widespread load-shedding, causing significant hardship for the general public.
Dr. Rahman stated that the energy shortage is severely impacting industrial production and business trade, while also driving up the prices of essential commodities.
The letter further highlights a deterioration in the overall socio-economic and law and order situation, which has pushed the population into extreme uncertainty.

As representatives of the people, the opposition leader emphasized that they cannot remain silent during such a crisis and that meaningful discussion in parliament is essential for an immediate solution.
Copies of the letter were also sent to the Prime Minister and the Parliament Secretariat to ensure the urgency of the matter is recognized.
caption:
Severe load-shedding and fuel shortages are crippling the country. Now, the opposition leader is demanding an urgent parliamentary session to find a solution.

Opposition leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Amir Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has written to Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed calling for a special session of the National Parliament.

The request comes amid a severe electricity and fuel crisis that has led to widespread load-shedding, causing significant hardship for the general public.

Dr. Rahman stated that the energy shortage is severely impacting industrial production and business trade, while also driving up the prices of essential commodities.

The letter further highlights a deterioration in the overall socio-economic and law and order situation, which has pushed the population into extreme uncertainty.

As representatives of the people, the opposition leader emphasized that they cannot remain silent during such a crisis and that meaningful discussion in parliament is essential for an immediate solution.

Copies of the letter were also sent to the Prime Minister and the Parliament Secretariat to ensure the urgency of the matter is recognized.
